newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL ROASTERS FINDING IT HARDER TO BUY COFFEE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL ROASTERS FINDING IT HARDER TO BUY COFFEE.

text.p: Brazilian coffee roasters are finding it increasingly difficult to get green coffee for roasting in the domestic market, according to an indicator drawn up by Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union.
The indicator works on a basis of one to 9, with nine representing the tightest supply.
For Aug 4-8, the indicator rose to 4.79 points, moving toward what is considered to be a critical area and confirming the tendency toward tighter supply which has been seen over the last four weeks.
At the same stage last year, the tendency as registered by the indicator was for increased supply to the market.
"Sellers (this year) are holding back coffee in the belief that the expectation of a smaller crop will push prices higher," union president Nathan Herszkowicz said in a statement.

"The consequences are a lack of supply, very high prices for the best coffees, making their use impossible for the industry, and offers of unsuitable coffees of bad quality which we have to reject," he added.

The higher green coffee prices run the risk of starting up a new cycle of price rises for the consumer and also of poorer quality as roasters will be pushed to use lower quality coffees in order to keep up and running.

"The reduced supply to the market is not justified by the time of the year and even less by the expectation of a small harvest given that any forecast at this stage is only speculation due to the absence of reliable surveys," he said.
Larger auctions of government coffee stocks are needed immediately to ease the supply situation, Herszkowicz said.
Also if recent requests for further producer were granted, this would only serve to aggravate the situation, he added.
"At this point, only Brazil has stocks to sell and should do so when it will not be competing with Colombian and Central American stocks," he said.
